report:
I'd merge this. I found nothing the contributor has to fix.

**Checks I ran**
- **Tests:** `pnpm vitest run packages/tailwindcss` passed: 42 files, 5017 tests passed, 1 skipped. That includes the new `anchor` and `anchored` tests and the updated IntelliSense snapshot, which now lists `anchor-none` and `anchored-auto`.
- **Formatting:** `npx prettier --check` on all four changed text files reported "All matched files use Prettier code style!"
- **Type check:** `npx tsc --noEmit` in `packages/tailwindcss` does report errors, but every one is in a file this PR doesn't touch (the browser, cli, standalone and upgrade packages, plus files that need the unbuilt `@tailwindcss/oxide`). None are in `src/utilities.ts`, `src/utilities.test.ts` or `src/property-order.ts`.

**Behaviour checked against the issue**
- **Named values:** `anchor-tooltip` gives `anchor-name: --tooltip`, and `anchored-menu` gives `position-anchor: --menu`.
- **Keywords:** `anchor-none` gives `none` and `anchored-auto` gives `auto`.
- **Arbitrary values pass through:** `anchor-[--a,--b]`, `anchor-[--a]`, `anchor-[var(--x)]`, `anchored-[--menu]`, `anchored-[none]` and `anchored-(--x)` (which gives `var(--x)`).
- **No CSS:** bare `anchor` and `anchored`, the negative forms (`-anchor-foo`, `-anchor-[--a]`), modifiers (`anchor-none/foo`, `anchor-[--a]/foo`, `anchor-1/2`), and values with other characters (`anchor-foo.bar`, `anchor-50%`).
- **Variants and `!important`:** `hover:` and `!` work.

I checked the edge cases above with a throwaway probe test, which I deleted afterwards. `git status` is the same as when I started: the 5 modified files and nothing untracked.

**Nits (not blocking)**
- The new `CHANGELOG.md` line has no PR link. Every other Unreleased entry ends with `([#NNNNN](https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/NNNNN))`.
- Keyword values swapped across the two utilities become dashed idents: `anchored-none` gives `position-anchor: --none` and `anchor-auto` gives `anchor-name: --auto`. That's allowed by the issue, but `anchored-none` could surprise people.
- `anchor--foo` gives `anchor-name: ---foo`. It's valid CSS but looks odd.
- The new `property-order.ts` entries (`anchor-name`, `position-anchor` after `position`) aren't asked for by the issue. They are needed so the new properties sort properly, so this isn't a scope problem.
